flags.title: Amazon edited the listing title; the stored wording and the live wording differ
flags.what: The Emeril Lagasse listing (B09B7SB46R) served 'Countertop Convection Cooker, 24 One-Touch Preset Options, Extra Large Interior, Six Cooking Accessories Included' on 2026-11-16. data/products.json and marketing/index.html still carry the 2026-11-13/14 wording ('French doors, 24 cooking functions, dual-speed fan and rotisserie for easy family meals'). The listing's own URL slug still contains 'dual-speed-rotisserie', so the live title and the live slug disagree with each other.
flags.why_it_matters: Any page that promises rotisserie or a dual-speed fan for this machine is quoting wording that is not in the title today. This site publishes neither.

flags.title: The release gate could not fail on disclosure, disclaimer, single-h1 or row-provenance — found by this session, fixed upstream while this PR was in flight
flags.what: tools/verify_site.py builds its 'owned pages' set from data/z3/build-manifest.json's 'files' values, but those values are 12-character content digests (e.g. agent-terms: 94cb0fee17a9), not paths. No page is ever matched, so V1/V2/V3/V4 findings are demoted to advisory for the whole repository. Reproduced on 2026-11-16 with a synthetic page missing the disclosure sentence and carrying an unsourced table row: those checks reported only as advisory and the exit code came from an unrelated 'sitemap.xml missing' error. UPDATE 2026-11-16, before merge: while this session was in flight, session 81bc99d0 landed exactly this fix on main (PR #112): the manifest gained explicit 'paths' and verify_site.py consumes them, so V1-V4 can now fail. Reproduced on the rebased tree.
flags.why_it_matters: 'VERIFY PASS' on this repository has been read as evidence that disclosure and row-provenance rules hold. It is not. The rules do hold today — this session checked them independently — but the gate would not have caught it if they did not.
flags.action: Upstream fix landed during this session: tools/build_site.py now records explicit output paths in data/z3/build-manifest.json and tools/verify_site.py consumes 'paths' before falling back to 'files', with scripts/test_manifest_regression.py as the regression test (commit f48ec8b, merged in PR #112). This session re-verified on the rebased tree: the gate now hard-fails on V1/V3/V4 for pages it owns and VERIFY PASS covers 106 pages. The compensating lint tools/cba81fa5_lint.py is kept - it covers site/**, which the audit generator's manifest does not own, so the two are complementary, not duplicate.

flags.title: Three reader sets, two brands, overlapping topics
flags.what: /read/ ('The Crisp Report', 11 pages, images, JSON-LD — session d18303ca), site/articles/ (4 feature articles: Sync Finish, the 26QT French door, the 450°F Hi-Fry button — same session, added to main while this session was in flight) and /site/ plus site/guides/ ('Air Fryer Field Notes', sessions 59d84c55 and cba81fa5, 5 guides) all answer shopper questions from the same three listings on the same day. read/capacity.html, site/guides/capacity-maths.html and articles/hi-fry-450.html are the clearest overlaps, as are the cleaning and best-seller pages.
flags.why_it_matters: A reader who finds both sees the same argument twice from two names, and search engines see two near-duplicate sets. The board has flagged duplicate registers for the same reason; this is the reader-facing version of it.
flags.action: Owner decision (question Q-12 in site/answers.html): adopt one brand as canonical, keep the others as internal verification, or merge the sets into one nav with one index. This session took the middle path: the root front door leads to read/ for reading and site/ for the evidence desk and the decision board, and site/guides/index.html labels itself a second-source check with the overlap named. Nothing was deleted, and all three sets are in site/site-index.json (18 pages) and the sitemap.

flags.title: The published home page was rendering a Python list as text — every gate passed it
flags.what:
scripts/build_site.py built the three home-page product cards by appending them to a list and then interpolating that list into the page template:
{product_cards}
. Python renders a list inside an f-string by repr(), so the live home page carried roughly a kilobyte of escaped repr text — ['<div class="pcard"><span class="pcard-brand">CHEFMAN · 6 Quart</span>…, '…'] — where three cards should have been. The cards' content, links and disclosure all remained in the file, which is why nothing caught it: the disclosure sentence was present, all 165 external links resolved, the HTML parsed, exactly one h1, no placeholder token, the sitemap covered the page. Verified on main at 6432f9a and in the live page.
flags.why_it_matters: This is the failure mode the whole brief is about, in the opposite direction from a hallucination: the facts were right, the presentation was broken, and a gate that only checks facts and links cannot see it. A reader who saw this would judge the site by it in about two seconds.
flags.action:
Fixed here, because leaving a broken home page published was the worse option: the template line is now
{''.join(product_cards)}
, matching how article_cards is built fifteen lines below. Regression test added: scripts/cba81fa5_test_no_repr_output.py scans every published page for the three signatures of a joined repr (['< , ', '< , ']) with script/pre/code stripped, and carries its own --selftest that proves it catches the symptom and ignores clean markup. The right permanent fix is a render-level check in the shared gates: assert the home page contains the expected number of .pcard elements and that no page contains a bracket-quote-tag sequence.

flags.title: This session's own front-door band shipped a malformed anchor, and it was visible on the live page
flags.what: The band's source citation was emitted with its title attribute *after* the closing angle bracket — <a href=… target=… rel=…>title="Amazon Associates Program Policies…">CBA-S09</a> — so the browser painted the literal text title="Amazon Associates Program Policies, Participation Requirements 2(b), read 2026-11-16" as prose in the band's fine print. Found by reading the deployed page after the merge, not by any gate. Fixed in tools/build_cba81fa5_site.py (attribute moved inside the tag), and the fine print now carries the exact required disclosure sentence, which a new rule checks.
flags.why_it_matters: It is the same class of defect as CBA-F-06 from the other direction: the facts, the links and the structure were all correct, and the page still read as broken to a human. Every existing gate passed it — the href resolved, the disclosure sentence existed elsewhere on the page, the HTML parsed. So the fix is not 'check the links harder': it is to scan for attribute text leaking outside a tag, which no gate did.
flags.action: Closed by this session: generator fixed; tools/cba81fa5_lint.py gained STYLE:malformed-tag, run over every page under site/ and over the band's own region in index.html, plus a band-specific check that the exact disclosure sentence appears inside the band rather than only in the page footer. Suggested for the shared gates: the same one-line pattern in tools/verify_site.py V7, since this defect class is generic.
